input.rationale: Spent the remaining budget on one bounded source check outside the feature audited so far: the network transport's heartbeat fast path, which invokes the Raft heartbeat handler from the transport goroutine rather than the main loop. The guard is conservative - a request is treated as a heartbeat only when it has a term, a leader address, zero previous-log index and term, no entries and a zero leader commit index - and the handler itself only handles AppendEntries and returns early when the node is shut down, so the fast path cannot append entries or apply committed entries off the main loop. I recorded that as a sourced negative rather than a suspicion, and no conclusion in the run changes.

knowledge.statement: The network transport routes an AppendEntries request to the heartbeat handler in its own goroutine only when the decoded request has a non-zero term, a leader address, zero PrevLogEntry and PrevLogTerm, no entries and a zero LeaderCommitIndex; every other AppendEntries request is dispatched to the Raft main loop. The handler accepts only AppendEntries commands and returns immediately when the node is shutting down, so the off-main-loop path cannot append entries or apply committed entries for the follower.
knowledge.conditions: NetworkTransport RPC decoding and dispatch; the equivalent InmemTransport does not implement the fast path (its SetHeartbeatHandler is a no-op), so this applies to the network transport only.

knowledge.statement: NewRaft's post-restore configuration scan iterates index from max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 up to the last log index and calls processConfigurationLogEntry for every entry in that range, so configuration entries at or below the scan start are never processed into r.configurations during construction.
knowledge.conditions: Construction of a Raft instance from retained log/stable/snapshot state; the scan runs after restoreSnapshot and after restoreFromCommittedLogs, and before skipStartup returns control to the caller.

history.conditions: Construction of a Raft instance from retained log/stable/snapshot state; the scan runs after restoreSnapshot and after restoreFromCommittedLogs, and before skipStartup returns control to the caller.

knowledge.statement: With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs true and a log store implementing CommitTrackingLogStore, restoreFromCommittedLogs sets the in-memory commit index from store.GetCommitIndex() (clamped to the log's last index) and calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs enqueues the corresponding commitTuples on fsmMutateCh and then sets lastApplied to that index.
knowledge.conditions: Called during NewRaft, after snapshot restore and before runFSM is started; the log store must implement CommitTrackingLogStore or NewRaft returns ErrIncompatibleLogStore.

knowledge.statement: Outside NewRaft, r.configurations is updated only by the AppendEntries path for entries that are not already present as duplicates with the same term, by processConfigurationLogEntry for those new entries, and by installSnapshot (which sets both latest and committed from the snapshot request); processLogs and the FSM apply path never update the configuration.
knowledge.conditions: Running follower/leader loops on the main thread; duplicate entries (index at or below lastLogIdx with matching term) are skipped before processConfigurationLogEntry is reached.

history.statement: Outside NewRaft, r.configurations is updated only by the AppendEntries path for entries that are not already present as duplicates with the same term, by processConfigurationLogEntry for those new entries, and by installSnapshot (which sets both latest and committed from the snapshot request); processLogs and the FSM apply path never update the configuration.
history.conditions: Running follower/leader loops on the main thread; duplicate entries (index at or below lastLogIdx with matching term) are skipped before processConfigurationLogEntry is reached.

knowledge.statement: A node's election quorum and voter eligibility are computed only from r.configurations.latest (quorumSize counts Voters in latest; the candidate threshold is grantedVotes >= quorumSize, and vote requests are admitted based on the receiver's own latest configuration), so a node holding a configuration older than its own committed log counts a smaller voter set and requires fewer votes to become leader.
knowledge.conditions: Election handling on the candidate and voter sides (runCandidate, requestVote); r.configurations.latest is not reconciled with the node's log at any other time.

history.conditions: Election handling on the candidate and voter sides (runCandidate, requestVote); r.configurations.latest is not reconciled with the node's log at any other time.

knowledge.statement: The persisted commit index that RestoreCommittedLogs later reads is written only by tryStageCommitIndex, which returns immediately unless r.RestoreCommittedLogs is true; its callers are dispatchLogs on a leader (staging the commit index as of before the new entries are stored) and the AppendEntries path on a follower (staging min(LeaderCommitIndex, last new entry index)). A node that committed entries while the feature was disabled leaves a stored commit index of 0, so a later restart with the feature enabled replays nothing even though its log is long.
knowledge.conditions: Requires a log store implementing CommitTrackingLogStore; the guard is on the running instance's RestoreCommittedLogs value, so mixed deployments (feature off, then on) do not have a persisted commit index to replay.

knowledge.statement: Two entries that end up at the same log index with the same term but different payloads on different servers are never reconciled by AppendEntries: the receiver truncates its suffix only when an incoming entry at an existing index has a different term, and an entry whose index and term match the stored one is skipped as a duplicate before any configuration or log processing, so the divergence persists while the cluster continues to commit later entries.
knowledge.conditions: AppendEntries conflict handling (raft.go 1526-1553) on a follower whose stored entry at that index has the same term; observed after the split-leader window of the RestoreCommittedLogs restart defect was healed with a further committed entry and, in a later receipt, after roughly two hundred further committed entries.

knowledge.statement: With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and a CommitTrackingLogStore, NewRaft cannot return when the replay must hand more batches to fsmMutateCh than that channel's 128-slot buffer holds, because the only consumer of the channel is runFSM, which NewRaft starts after the replay returns; the number of batches is ceil(committed-but-unapplied entries / MaxAppendEntries), so 129 entries above the last applied index stall the constructor with MaxAppendEntries 1 and 8193 entries do so with the default 64. Entries that never reach the FSM commit path (LogNoop) are skipped by prepareLog and do not create batches.

knowledge.statement: On a follower that receives an InstallSnapshot, the handler streams and finalises the snapshot, restores the FSM through fsmMutateCh, sets lastApplied and the last snapshot to the request's last log index and term, and replaces the latest and committed configuration from the request; the local log is then either removed entirely (monotonic stores) or compacted up to the snapshot index. A follower that has fallen behind a leader whose log was compacted is therefore sent a snapshot and ends up with the leader's FSM state, entry suffix and configuration, replacing any divergent entry it held at an index the leader also used.
knowledge.conditions: Triggered either because the leader can no longer serve the entries the follower needs (its log was compacted past the follower's position) or because the leader consumed a snapshot through the Restore contract and pushed it to its followers; observed with in-memory stores in both cases.

history.statement: On a follower that receives an InstallSnapshot, the handler streams and finalises the snapshot, restores the FSM through fsmMutateCh, sets lastApplied and the last snapshot to the request's last log index and term, and replaces the latest and committed configuration from the request; the local log is then either removed entirely (monotonic stores) or compacted up to the snapshot index. A follower that has fallen behind a leader whose log was compacted is therefore sent a snapshot and ends up with the leader's FSM state, entry suffix and configuration, replacing any divergent entry it held at an index the leader also used.
history.conditions: Follower receives InstallSnapshot because the leader can no longer serve the entries it needs (its log was compacted past the follower's position); observed with in-memory stores after the stale-configuration split was healed, where the leader snapshotted with TrailingLogs 0 and the disconnected node was then reconnected.

knowledge.statement: The snapshot loop treats a failed snapshot creation as a logged error and keeps running: when takeSnapshot returns an error other than ErrNothingNewToSnapshot the loop logs it and continues, so a node whose snapshot store keeps failing retains its last successful snapshot and its log grows without bound relative to it.
knowledge.conditions: Running leader or follower with a caller-provided SnapshotStore whose Create fails; observed through a wrapper store whose Create fails after the node's first snapshot, with four failed attempts while thousands of entries were committed.

knowledge.statement: A candidate is granted votes only if its log is at least as up to date as the voter's: requestVote rejects a candidate whose last log term is lower, or whose last log index is smaller at the same term. Consequently, once an entry at an index has been committed in term T by a leader whose log was the most up to date, any later leader must have a log whose last entry is at least as up to date, so it can only append entries beyond that index and cannot replace the entry at it with a different term; the entry can only be replaced by a snapshot install or a user restore.
knowledge.conditions: Voter-side vote admission (raft.go 1725-1750) applied to the split-brain state of this defect, where the conflicting entries are at the highest index of every log and at the same term.

knowledge.statement: The repository's own tests for Config.RestoreCommittedLogs exercise a single-node cluster that commits commands, takes a snapshot and restarts the node, asserting only that the FSM is replayed up to the log store's commit index and that the commit index sits between the snapshot index and the last log index; no test constructs a restart whose snapshot predates a committed configuration entry, and none observes the configuration or quorum the restarted node uses. The user-restore path is covered by snapshotAndRestore, which opens a snapshot, calls Restore on the leader and asserts that the FSM contents are reverted and that all nodes agree.
knowledge.conditions: Read of the target's test sources in the captured snapshot; test expectations describe the scenarios those tests construct, not the library's full contract.
